public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 337

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/337](https://www.erdosproblems.com/337)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [ErGr80b] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L., *On bases with an exact order*. Acta Arith. (1980),
  201-207.
- [RT85] Ruzsa, I. Z. and Turjányi, S., *A note on additive bases of integers*. Publ. Math.
  Debrecen (1985), 101-104.
- [Tu84] Turjányi, S., *A note on basis sequences*. Topics in classical number theory, Vol. I, II
  (Budapest, 1981) (1984), 1571-1576.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos337

open Filter Set Asymptotics

open scoped Pointwise

/--
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be an additive basis (of any finite order) such that
$\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert=o(N)$. Is it true that
$$
\lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{\lvert (A+A)\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}
{\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}=\infty?
$$

The answer is no, and a counterexample was provided by Turjányi [Tu84]. This was generalised (to
the replacement of $A+A$ by the $h$-fold sumset $hA$ for any $h\geq 2$) by Ruzsa and Turjányi
[RT85].

"Additive basis" is `Set.IsAsymptoticAddBasis`: some finite $h$ has $hA$ containing every
sufficiently large integer. The exact notion `Set.IsAddBasis`, which asks that $hA$ be all of
$\mathbb{N}$, would force $0, 1 \in A$ and is not the class these results are about.

The linked file states the basis hypothesis as `∃ N₀, Set.Ici N₀ ⊆ iterated_sumset A k` and
indexes both counting functions by a real $x$ through $\lfloor x\rfloor$, where the counting
functions here are indexed by $N : \mathbb{N}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/68da20b96673899166e94638f5a7fffeb7231d35/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos337.lean"]
theorem erdos_337 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAsymptoticAddBasis →
      (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)) →
      Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ (((A + A) ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ) / ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ))
        atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
This was generalised (to the replacement of $A+A$ by the $h$-fold sumset $hA$ for any $h\geq 2$)
by Ruzsa and Turjányi [RT85].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_337.variants.h_fold : ∀ h : ℕ, 2 ≤ h →
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAsymptoticAddBasis ∧
      (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)) ∧
      ¬ Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
          ((h • A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ) / ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ))
        atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa and Turjányi do prove (under the same hypotheses) that
$$
\lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{\lvert (A+A+A)\cap \{1,\ldots,3N\}\rvert}
{\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}=\infty,
$$
and conjecture that the same should be true with $(A+A)\cap \{1,\ldots,2N\}$ in the numerator.

This follows from the Plünnecke–Ruzsa inequality applied to $B=A\cap\{0,\ldots,N\}$: if $A$ is a
basis of order $h$ then $hB$ contains every element of $\{N_0,\ldots,N\}$, so
$(\lvert B+B\rvert/\lvert B\rvert)^h\geq \lvert hB\rvert/\lvert B\rvert\gg N/\lvert B\rvert$,
which tends to infinity since $\lvert B\rvert=o(N)$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/9e4cd5617edacb313fb1da32adb4751f1fa8f603/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/337.lean#L95"]
theorem erdos_337.variants.ruzsa_turjanyi :
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAsymptoticAddBasis →
      (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)) →
      Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
          (((A + A) ∩ Icc 1 (2 * N)).ncard : ℝ) / ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ))
        atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa and Turjányi do prove (under the same hypotheses) that
$$
\lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{\lvert (A+A+A)\cap \{1,\ldots,3N\}\rvert}
{\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}=\infty.
$$

This is weaker than `Erdos337.erdos_337.variants.ruzsa_turjanyi`: translating by a fixed
$a\in A$ with $1\leq a\leq N$ embeds $(A+A)\cap\{1,\ldots,2N\}$ into
$(A+A+A)\cap\{1,\ldots,3N\}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/9e4cd5617edacb313fb1da32adb4751f1fa8f603/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/337.lean#L240"]
theorem erdos_337.variants.three_fold :
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAsymptoticAddBasis →
      (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)) →
      Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
          (((A + A + A) ∩ Icc 1 (3 * N)).ncard : ℝ) / ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ))
        atTop atTop := by
  sorry

end Erdos337

reformulations.difference: The Lean hypothesis is `Set.IsAsymptoticAddBasis A`: for some n, every sufficiently large integer is a sum of EXACTLY n elements of A, and 0 ∈ A is not required. The cited original source [ErGr80b] (Acta Arith. 37, 201–207) defines an asymptotic basis of order r as 'every sufficiently large integer is the sum of AT MOST r elements of A'. RT85 instead assumes 0 ∈ A. These classes differ: A = {n ≡ 1 mod 3} is an at-most-3 basis but not an exactly-n basis for any n. The counting functions are indexed by N : ℕ, where the linked formal proof uses a real x through ⌊x⌋₊.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The Lean class is contained in the at-most class, so a Lean-class counterexample is also a source-class counterexample. Conversely, suppose A is an at-most-r basis with A(N)=o(N) whose ratio does not tend to ∞. Put A₀ = A ∪ {0}. Then r•A₀ contains every large n (pad with zeros), so A₀ is in the Lean class. A₀ ∩ [1,N] = A ∩ [1,N], and (A₀+A₀) ∩ [1,N] ⊆ ((A+A) ∪ A) ∩ [1,N], so ratio_{A₀}(N) ≤ ratio_A(N) + 1. Hence A₀ is also a counterexample, and ∃-counterexample holds in one class iff in the other. Adding 0 and {1,…,N₀} to reach the exact notion `IsAddBasis`, or removing 0 to get A ⊆ ℤ_{>0}, likewise changes the ratio only by a bounded amount. So the answer (no) is the same under every notion. Turjányi's own definition (Zbl 0548.10039: hA ⊇ ℕ ∩ [N,∞), A ⊆ ℕ₀) is literally the repo's. For the ℕ vs ℝ indexing: I proved in Lean that the pinned plby theorem `not_erdos_337` (real-indexed, `Ici N₀ ⊆ iterated_sumset A k`) implies exactly this declaration's statement. The `IsAsymptoticAddBasis` hypothesis was unfolded, which is `Iff.rfl`; the bridge uses only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

reformulations.difference: This is a universal statement over the Lean basis class (exactly-n summands, 0 ∈ A not required). The source's hypotheses ('the same hypotheses': an additive basis in the at-most sense of ErGr80b, or with 0 ∈ A as in RT85) describe a larger class. So the Lean claim is formally weaker. The same applies to `three_fold`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let A be an at-most-r basis with A(N)=o(N). Then A₀ = A ∪ {0} is in the Lean class with A₀(N)=A(N). Applying the Lean statement to A₀ gives |((A+A) ∪ A) ∩ [1,2N]|/A(N) → ∞. Fix a ∈ A with a ≥ 1. Since A + a ⊆ A + A, we get |(A+A) ∩ [1,2N]| ≥ A(2N) − a. Hence |(A+A) ∩ [1,2N]| ≥ (|((A+A) ∪ A) ∩ [1,2N]| − a)/2, and the ratio for A also tends to ∞. For the 3-fold version, use 2A + a ⊆ 3A and A + 2a ⊆ 3A the same way. In any case the Plünnecke–Ruzsa argument proves both statements directly for the larger class. So the Lean and source versions are equivalent (both true).

review.notes:
No misformalizations found. All four declarations are faithful, and I believe all four are true.

(1) `erdos_337`: the `answer(False)` polarity is correct (the source asks "Is it true that lim = ∞?", and the answer is no). The hypotheses are satisfiable, for example by the squares, so the right-hand side is not vacuous. The ratio's division by zero can only happen at finitely many N. The `formal_proof using lean4` record is valid: the pinned plby file compiles in this environment, `not_erdos_337` uses only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], and I proved in a scratch file a bridge theorem showing it implies this declaration's statement. The docstring's description of the linked file is accurate.

(2) `h_fold`: `h • A` elaborates to `Set.NSMul`, the h-fold sumset. It is not the dilation {h·a}; the dilation reading would have made the statement trivial. The ∀h ∃A quantifier order matches RT85 (a separate basis, of order h+1, for each h). `¬Tendsto … atTop atTop` is equivalent to RT's liminf < ∞.

(3) `ruzsa_turjanyi`: erdosproblems.com (snapshot 2026-08-24, including its single forum comment) records this only as a conjecture of RT85 and says nothing about a resolution. The file tags it `research solved` and sketches a Plünnecke–Ruzsa proof. I checked that argument and it is correct: B = A ∩ [0,N], hB ⊇ [N₀,N], |hB| ≤ (|2B|/|B|)^h |B|, and 2B ⊆ (A+A) ∩ [0,2N]. So the file is ahead of the source, not stale; I did not file a status issue. Erdosproblems.com may want to record the resolution.

(4) `three_fold`: RT85's theorem (2). The docstring's claim that it follows from `ruzsa_turjanyi` via translation by a fixed a ∈ A is correct.

Linking fork commits with the `formal_conjectures` kind is common in this repository (about 80 links to mo271's fork alone), so I did not flag it.
